precepts.text: David says the Lord is my rock, and then the God of my rock; in him will I trust.
precepts.point: David distinguishes the Lord my rock from the God of my rock, just as he says, the Lord said unto my Lord: David understood before anybody else that the head of Christ is God. You have our Rock, and you have the God of our Rock, which is the Father.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
David distinguishes two: “The Lord is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; The God of my rock; in him will I trust”. There is the Lord my rock, and there is the God of my rock. You have our Rock, which is Christ, and you have the God of our Rock, which is the Father.

David understood that difference before anybody else. The Rock that begat Israel, the one we are unmindful of, is Christ, and above him is his God.

precepts.text: The Lord thundered from heaven, and the most High uttered his voice; he sent out arrows, and scattered them; lightning, and discomfited them, the same word used of the Philistines at Mizpeh.
precepts.point: Samuel was one of the most respected prophets in the whole history of the prophets: he established the kingdom and anointed Saul, and by his faithfulness he was found a true prophet. Faithfulness translates loyalty. He came up under Eli, watched Eli's sons go wicked, Eli die, and the nation take losses, but Samuel stayed loyal to the Most High, just as Abraham's faith was tried again and again and he remained faithful.

note.label: 1 Samuel 7: Put Away the Strange Gods, and the Lord Thundered

precepts.why:
“The Lord thundered from heaven, and the most High uttered his voice. And he sent out arrows, and scattered them; lightning, and discomfited them.”

Discomfited: the same word used of the Philistines at Mizpeh, where “the Lord thundered with a great thunder on that day upon the Philistines, and discomfited them.” The thunder is the voice of the Most High, and when he utters it in the battle his enemies are scattered.

Keep the commandments and send up that prayer, and the Most High will come down in thunder against your enemies.

precepts.text: The Lord thundered from heaven, and the most High uttered his voice; imagine how terrified they were when that voice went off.
precepts.point: Is it not wheat harvest today? To demonstrate how wicked Israel was for asking a king, Samuel calls unto the Lord for thunder and rain on the very day they expected clear skies to gather the wheat. The Lord sent thunder and rain that day, and all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
To demonstrate how wicked Israel was for asking a king, Samuel asks, “Is it not wheat harvest to day?” That was the very day they expected clear skies to gather the wheat, and Samuel called unto the Lord, “and the Lord sent thunder and rain that day”.

“The Lord thundered from heaven, and the most High uttered his voice.” Imagine how terrified they were when that voice went off over their harvest: “all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel.”

precepts.text: And he sent out arrows, and scattered them; lightning, and discomfited them; that is the power the Most High put on display.
precepts.point: Is it not wheat harvest today? To demonstrate how wicked Israel was for asking a king, Samuel calls unto the Lord for thunder and rain on the very day they expected clear skies to gather the wheat. The Lord sent thunder and rain that day, and all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
“And he sent out arrows, and scattered them; lightning, and discomfited them.” That is the power the Most High put on display that day.

The thunder and rain came when Samuel called, on the day it should have been clear, “that ye may perceive and see that your wickedness is great, which ye have done in the sight of the Lord, in asking you a king.”

precepts.text: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart, and lean not unto thine own understanding.
precepts.point: This is heavy: like Judas Maccabee, Simon, Jonathan and all our forefathers, the first thing David did in trouble was turn to the Most High. They trusted in God and not in man. Today many of our people have it backwards; they trust in a vote and in man and then call on God.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.”

David sang this song “in the day that the Lord had delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul”: “The Lord is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; The God of my rock; in him will I trust”. He called the Lord his shield, the horn of his salvation, his high tower, his refuge and his saviour: “thou savest me from violence.”

This is heavy. Like Judas Maccabee, Simon, Jonathan and all our forefathers, the first thing David did in trouble was turn to the Most High. They trusted in God and not in man. Today many of our people have it backwards: they trust in a vote and in man, and then call on God.

precepts.text: The Lord came down in the pillar of the cloud and stood in the door of the tabernacle; he came down in a cloud to speak, just as David describes.
precepts.point: The Most High sent out arrows and lightning and scattered his enemies, and the channels of the sea and the foundations of the world were discovered at the rebuking of the Lord, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils. His power over creation is total.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“And the Lord came down in the pillar of the cloud, and stood in the door of the tabernacle, and called Aaron and Miriam”. He came down in a cloud to speak, just as David describes.

David sang, “He bowed the heavens also, and came down; and darkness was under his feet. And he rode upon a cherub, and did fly: and he was seen upon the wings of the wind. And he made darkness pavilions round about him, dark waters, and thick clouds of the skies.” That is how the Most High travels, shielded in the darkness of the cloud, the same way he came down and spoke to Moses face to face.

precepts.text: When he uttereth his voice there is a multitude of waters in the heavens; he maketh lightnings with rain and bringeth forth the wind out of his treasures.
precepts.point: The Most High sent out arrows and lightning and scattered his enemies, and the channels of the sea and the foundations of the world were discovered at the rebuking of the Lord, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils. His power over creation is total.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“He hath made the earth by his power, he hath established the world by his wisdom, and hath stretched out the heavens by his discretion. When he uttereth his voice, there is a multitude of waters in the heavens”, and “he maketh lightnings with rain, and bringeth forth the wind out of his treasures.”

David sang, “The Lord thundered from heaven, and the most High uttered his voice. And he sent out arrows, and scattered them; lightning, and discomfited them.” What we hear as thunder is the Most High speaking. Esau says the thunder is only clouds clashing; the scripture says it is the voice of the Lord, and after his voice there is a multitude of waters, meaning the rain that follows.

The one who made the earth by his power rules all of it: “the channels of the sea appeared, the foundations of the world were discovered, at the rebuking of the Lord, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils.” His power over creation is total.

precepts.text: A voice came from heaven, and the people that stood by said it thundered; Christ said the voice came not because of him but for their sakes, showing the thunder was the Most High speaking.
precepts.point: The Most High sent out arrows and lightning and scattered his enemies, and the channels of the sea and the foundations of the world were discovered at the rebuking of the Lord, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils. His power over creation is total.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
Christ prayed, “Father, glorify thy name. Then came there a voice from heaven, saying, I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again. The people therefore, that stood by, and heard it, said that it thundered: others said, An angel spake to him. Jesus answered and said, This voice came not because of me, but for your sakes.”

The people heard the voice of the Father and called it thunder. That shows the thunder is the Most High speaking, just as David sang, “The Lord thundered from heaven, and the most High uttered his voice.” We hear it, but we cannot comprehend it because we no longer have that spirit upon us.

precepts.text: We dwell in the midst of a rebellious house, having eyes to see and see not, ears to hear and hear not; this is why we cannot understand the Lord's voice in the thunder.
precepts.point: The Most High sent out arrows and lightning and scattered his enemies, and the channels of the sea and the foundations of the world were discovered at the rebuking of the Lord, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils. His power over creation is total.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“Son of man, thou dwellest in the midst of a rebellious house, which have eyes to see, and see not; they have ears to hear, and hear not: for they are a rebellious house.”

That is why we cannot understand the Lord’s voice in the thunder. The Lord thunders from heaven and the Most High utters his voice, but we dwell in the midst of a rebellious house, with ears to hear that hear not. We no longer have that spirit upon us, so his voice sounds like clouds clashing, the way Esau tells it.

precepts.text: The Lord said, Verily I will cause the enemy to entreat thee well in the time of evil; the Most High delivers those he delights in.
precepts.point: The Lord rewarded David according to his righteousness and the cleanness of his hands, for he kept the ways of the Lord and did not wickedly depart from his God; all the Lord's judgments were before him and he did not depart from his statutes. He kept himself from his own iniquity, holding back his flesh; the one time it overtook him he was judged and got right back on track, for a righteous man falls and rises again.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“The Lord said, Verily it shall be well with thy remnant; verily I will cause the enemy to entreat thee well in the time of evil and in the time of affliction.” The Most High delivers those he delights in.

David sang, “He delivered me from my strong enemy, and from them that hated me: for they were too strong for me. They prevented me in the day of my calamity: but the Lord was my stay.” And, “He brought me forth also into a large place: he delivered me, because he delighted in me.”

The enemy was too strong for David, but in the time of evil the Lord was his stay and his help. When your ways please the Lord, he will deliver you.

precepts.text: God resisteth the proud but giveth grace unto the humble; submit yourselves to God, resist the devil, draw nigh to God, cleanse your hands and purify your hearts, the very thing we need in these last days.
precepts.point: The Lord rewarded David according to his righteousness and the cleanness of his hands, for he kept the ways of the Lord and did not wickedly depart from his God; all the Lord's judgments were before him and he did not depart from his statutes. He kept himself from his own iniquity, holding back his flesh; the one time it overtook him he was judged and got right back on track, for a righteous man falls and rises again.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble. Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.”

David sang, “The Lord rewarded me according to my righteousness: according to the cleanness of my hands hath he recompensed me. For I have kept the ways of the Lord, and have not wickedly departed from my God.” All the Lord’s judgments were before him, and he did not depart from his statutes. His hands were clean, and the Lord delivered him.

Submit to God, resist the devil, draw nigh to God, cleanse your hands and purify your hearts: that is the very thing we need in these last days.

precepts.text: A just man falleth seven times and riseth up again; that is what David did after his fall.
precepts.point: The Lord rewarded David according to his righteousness and the cleanness of his hands, for he kept the ways of the Lord and did not wickedly depart from his God; all the Lord's judgments were before him and he did not depart from his statutes. He kept himself from his own iniquity, holding back his flesh; the one time it overtook him he was judged and got right back on track, for a righteous man falls and rises again.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again”. That is what David did after his fall.

David held back his flesh. The one time it overtook him he was judged, and he got right back on track, for a righteous man falls and rises again. So he could still sing, “Therefore the Lord hath recompensed me according to my righteousness; according to my cleanness in his eye sight.”

precepts.text: Go not after thy lusts, but refrain thyself from thine appetites; David kept himself back from his iniquity all his days.
precepts.point: The Lord rewarded David according to his righteousness and the cleanness of his hands, for he kept the ways of the Lord and did not wickedly depart from his God; all the Lord's judgments were before him and he did not depart from his statutes. He kept himself from his own iniquity, holding back his flesh; the one time it overtook him he was judged and got right back on track, for a righteous man falls and rises again.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“Go not after thy lusts, but refrain thyself from thine appetites.” David kept himself back from his iniquity all his days.

That is what he meant when he sang, “I was also upright before him, and have kept myself from mine iniquity.” He refrained himself and held back his flesh, and the Lord recompensed him for it.

precepts.text: He shall have judgment without mercy that hath shewed no mercy, and mercy rejoiceth against judgment; we rejoice when mercy is extended in the day we deserved punishment.
precepts.point: The afflicted people the Most High saves, but his eyes are upon the haughty to bring them down. The afflicted is Israel. He is David's lamp and lightens his darkness, for by the Most High David ran through a troop, a body of some two hundred men or more.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“For he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment.”

David sang, “With the merciful thou wilt shew thyself merciful, and with the upright man thou wilt shew thyself upright. With the pure thou wilt shew thyself pure; and with the froward thou wilt shew thyself unsavoury.” What a man soweth, that shall he reap.

We all need mercy, so we must show mercy to one another, forgiving and not bearing grudges, that the Lord be merciful with us in the day of judgment. And we rejoice when mercy is extended in the day we deserved punishment.

precepts.text: The Most High will return to his place till they acknowledge their offence and seek his face in their affliction; the afflicted people is Israel.
precepts.point: The afflicted people the Most High saves, but his eyes are upon the haughty to bring them down. The afflicted is Israel. He is David's lamp and lightens his darkness, for by the Most High David ran through a troop, a body of some two hundred men or more.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” The afflicted people is Israel.

David sang, “And the afflicted people thou wilt save: but thine eyes are upon the haughty, that thou mayest bring them down.” Israel is the people the Most High leaves in affliction till they acknowledge their offence and seek his face, and it is the afflicted people he saves.

“For thou art my lamp, O Lord: and the Lord will lighten my darkness. For by thee I have run through a troop”: a troop is a body of some two hundred men or more.

precepts.text: The Lord is great and greatly to be praised, to be feared above all gods, for all the gods of the nations are idols but the Lord made the heavens; there is no other God.
precepts.point: The Most High made David's feet like hinds' feet and set him upon high places, and taught his hands to war so that a bow of steel is broken by his arms, not bent but broken. He gave David the shield of his salvation and his gentleness made him great; his repentance enlarged his steps so his feet did not slip. David knew a lion and a bear were nothing to a man trained by the Most High.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“For the Lord is great, and greatly to be praised: he is to be feared above all gods. For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.” There is no other God.

David sang, “As for God, his way is perfect; the word of the Lord is tried: he is a buckler to all them that trust in him. For who is God, save the Lord? and who is a rock, save our God?” A buckler is a shield. There is no other God save the Lord, and no rock save our God.

This is the answer to the Muslims and Negroes practicing Islam who try to make this rock into a cobblestone. It is talking about the Most High God of Israel, not a stone. The gods of the nations are idols; the Lord made the heavens.

precepts.text: Jeshurun waxed fat and kicked, forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation; that is what Israel did.
precepts.point: The Most High made David's feet like hinds' feet and set him upon high places, and taught his hands to war so that a bow of steel is broken by his arms, not bent but broken. He gave David the shield of his salvation and his gentleness made him great; his repentance enlarged his steps so his feet did not slip. David knew a lion and a bear were nothing to a man trained by the Most High.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked: thou art waxen fat, thou art grown thick, thou art covered with fatness; then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation.” That is what Israel did.

David knew where his strength came from: “God is my strength and power: and he maketh my way perfect.” This is what Israel forgot. We waxed fat and kicked, forgot the Most High and where our strength came from, and began to say we are lords ourselves.

But our strength comes from the Most High, who is merciful enough to let us take a breath and blink our eyes every moment.

precepts.text: As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen; he played with lions as with kids and bears as with lambs, and slew a giant when he was young, for he called upon the most high Lord who gave him strength.
precepts.point: The Most High made David's feet like hinds' feet and set him upon high places, and taught his hands to war so that a bow of steel is broken by his arms, not bent but broken. He gave David the shield of his salvation and his gentleness made him great; his repentance enlarged his steps so his feet did not slip. David knew a lion and a bear were nothing to a man trained by the Most High.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Israel. He played with lions as with kids, and with bears as with lambs. Slew he not a giant, when he was yet but young?” And “he called upon the most high Lord; and he gave him strength in his right hand to slay that mighty warrior, and set up the horn of his people.”

That is the man who sang, “He teacheth my hands to war; so that a bow of steel is broken by mine arms.” Not bent, but broken. David knew a lion and a bear were nothing to a man trained by the Most High.

The Most High made David’s feet “like hinds’ feet” and set him upon high places. He gave him “the shield of thy salvation: and thy gentleness hath made me great.” His repentance enlarged his steps, “so that my feet did not slip.”

precepts.text: The secrets of wisdom are double to that which is; the scriptures often carry a double meaning, speaking of that time and of what is to come.
precepts.point: David is prophesying, for this song is twofold; it speaks of David in that moment and of us who are yet to come. The Most High requires of us far less than our iniquity deserves: to repent, keep the commandments, and keep the faith in his son Jesus the Christ. For this David gives thanks among the heathen and sings praises unto the name of the Lord, who shows mercy to his anointed, to David and to his seed for evermore.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is! Know therefore that God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth.” The secrets of wisdom are double to that which is: the scriptures often carry a double meaning, speaking of that time and of what is to come.

David’s song is twofold, and David is prophesying. “It is God that avengeth me, and that bringeth down the people under me, And that bringeth me forth from mine enemies”: it speaks of David in that moment and of us who are yet to come.

And God exacteth of us less than our iniquity deserves. The Most High requires of us far less: to repent, keep the commandments, and keep the faith in his son Jesus the Christ. For this David gives thanks “among the heathen” and sings praises unto his name, for “He is the tower of salvation for his king: and sheweth mercy to his anointed, unto David, and to his seed for evermore.”
